assertions.claim: tools/runner refuses a lane whose declared --ram-mb does not fit the host before spawning anything: exit 3, 'ARBITER REFUSED' on stderr naming 'row stays dispatchable', no process spawned (ram-policy.md §4.1 / ORC-GD-3 / INV-3).
assertions.how_it_can_fail: Seeded defect: a mutated copy of tools/runner with `_arbiter_decide`'s condition `if projected_mb >= ARBITER_RESERVE_MB:` replaced by `if True:` admits the same candidate. The standalone --arbiter-admit check then observes exit 0 and `"admit": true` where it requires exit 3 and `"admit": false` — the assertion flips from PASS to FAIL.

green.evidence: "admit": false on stdout; 'ARBITER REFUSED' + 'row stays dispatchable' on stderr

green_full_launch.instrument: full launch --ram-mb 4608 under injected avail 5000 MB, child would write a marker file
green_full_launch.evidence: marker file absent — nothing was spawned

red.instrument: same standalone --arbiter-admit against the seeded-admit mutant
red.evidence: "admit": true — the assertion detects the regression

assertions.claim: A silent child that outlives --max-wall is terminated with exit 124, the kill line names the wall ceiling, and the run record stamps killed_by == "wall" (attributable).
assertions.how_it_can_fail: Seeded defect: a mutated copy with the fallback wall condition `elif args.max_wall and elapsed >= args.max_wall:` disabled to `elif args.max_wall and False:` lets the child run to completion. The check then observes exit 0 where it requires 124.

green.evidence: 'wall ceiling 2s' kill line; run record killed_by == "wall"

red.instrument: --max-wall 1 -- python3 sleep(3) against the seeded wall-disabled mutant
red.evidence: child completed; no kill line — the assertion detects the regression

assertions.claim: Under sustained kernel memory pressure (injected level 4), the L3 backstop ALARMS, names the largest host-wide consumer, records host_alarms on the run record, and NEVER kills: the child completes with exit 0 (ram-policy.md §4.2 INV-1 / §4.3-4.4 — the T821 replacement for the deleted host-guard kill).
assertions.how_it_can_fail: Seeded defect: a mutated copy re-introduces a kill verb on the pressure alarm (`kill_reason` set when the alarm fires). The check then observes exit 124 and a `[runner] KILL:` line where it requires exit 0 and no kill — the 'never kills' assertion detects exactly the INV-1 regression T821 deleted.

green.evidence: 'ALARM: host memory pressure level 4 sustained' + 'never killed' on stderr; run record host_alarms[] with level 4 and a named consumer; no `[runner] KILL:` line

red.instrument: same, against the seeded kill-on-pressure mutant
red.evidence: a `[runner] KILL:` line appeared — the assertion detects the regression

assertions.claim: A dispatch writes its run record to the bare untracked/runs/<task>.json path that `reap` keys on, with run_kind == "dispatch" and a non-empty run_kind_reason (T895 — the kind is stated by the writer, never inferred by a reader).
assertions.how_it_can_fail: Seeded defect: a mutated copy drops the `"run_kind": run_kind,` entry from the launch record. The check then reads run_kind == null where it requires "dispatch".

green.instrument: MANAGENT_TASK_ID set, child python3 print + exit 0
green.evidence: untracked/runs/<task>.json present with run_kind == "dispatch" and non-empty run_kind_reason

red.instrument: same, against the seeded kind-less-record mutant
red.evidence: record present but run_kind == null — the assertion detects the regression

not_covered.why: That is bin/subagent behaviour (`_wall_band_ram_mb` / `_declared_ram_mb`), not a tools/runner surface. tools/runner RECEIVES the already-resolved --ram-mb; it contains no band table to assert. The band arithmetic and its boundaries are already covered by tools/regression-ram-declaration.sh (T913), which drives the real bin/subagent --dry-run path and asserts 59/60/599/600/1799/1800/10800 s. Duplicating it here would assert a file that is not the module under test.

not_covered.item: Assertion #4's literal 'host guard kills the lane' wording from the brief
not_covered.why: That wording describes the T362 host-guard KILL, which T821 DELETED (ram-policy.md §6 items 1-6; the floor's 16-of-20 futile kills). The current L3 backstop alarms and never kills. A4 asserts the current semantics and, as its red control, seeds the exact kill-on-pressure defect that a regression back toward the deleted guard would reintroduce.
